**The document does not report GPT-4 accuracy with 30 documents.**

- **Only a subset was tested.** GPT-4 (8K) was evaluated only "on a subset of multi-document QA experiments," because running the full experiments would cost more than $6000 (p. 4, footnote 6).
- **That subset used 20 documents.** It was "500 random multi-document QA examples with 20 total documents in each input context" (p. 15, Appendix D).
- **No exact numbers are given in the text, even for 20 documents.** The paper says only that GPT-4 "achieves higher absolute performance than any other language model, but still shows a U-shaped performance curve" (p. 15). The specific values appear only in Figure 15, which isn't readable here.
- **The 30-document table has no GPT-4 row.** Table 7 lists only Claude-1.3, Claude-1.3 (100K), GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K), MPT-30B-Instruct and LongChat-13B (16K) (p. 18).

If a 30-document comparison is useful, the best result in Table 7 is GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K): 73.4% when the answer document comes first, falling to 50.5% at index 9 (p. 18).
